coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: PG&E Southern Switchyard (outside the project boundary; not part of redevelopment)
record.summary: The PG&E Southern Switchyard, one of two PG&E electrical switchyards at the western end of the Potrero Power Station site, shown on the Design for Development's site-boundary figure outside the project site boundary. The other, the roughly 4.8-acre 'PG&E Northern Switchyard' at the corner of 22nd and Illinois Streets, owned and operated by PG&E, is inside the dashed 29-acre planning-area boundary but outside the 21-acre parcel the developer owns and outside the Development Agreement's jurisdiction (this dataset shows that area as Blocks 13 and 14).

notes.accuracy_caveat: LOW CONFIDENCE, DIRECTIONAL ONLY -- this is a materially weaker approximation than this site's numbered blocks. This polygon marks the PG&E Southern Switchyard, which the final D4D (p.12, Figure 1.2.1) places outside the project site boundary, between Humboldt and 23rd Streets west of Block 5. The 4.8-acre PG&E parcel at 22nd and Illinois that public reporting and SF Planning describe is the separate Northern Switchyard, which is inside the project boundary and is not what this polygon shows (this dataset represents that area as Blocks 13 and 14). This polygon's reshaped area is ~4.6 acres, but the D4D gives no area for the Southern Switchyard, so that figure is not a check against anything. The D4D diagram does not further subdivide this area (it is entirely outside the project site boundary, so the D4D had no reason to draw its actual fenceline), so the true switchyard footprint may still differ in detail from this trace. Treat this polygon as marking the correct general block and rough shape (including wrapping around Block 5's south side to 23rd St/Georgia Lane), not the switchyard's real surveyed boundary.
notes.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (p.245).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: No DataSF Assessor parcel search (by address, by zoning code, or by proximity) turned up a distinctly-shaped, plausibly-switchyard-sized real parcel here -- DataSF's parcel records in this area are either large undifferentiated placeholder shapes (shared across many of this site's D4D blocks, per this dataset's other Potrero entries) or small unrelated lots. Real ownership and the 'not part of the sale' status are well-documented in secondary sources, but a precise Assessor-parcel-level boundary was not found. (This is Pier & Point's own parcel search, not something the cited Design for Development can establish; the D4D does not address Assessor parcels.) The 2018 draft EIR (Vol. 1, Ch. 2) describes the 4.8-acre PG&E sub-area (the Northern Switchyard) as a portion of Assessor's Block 4175/Lot 018, so an Assessor lot reference exists for that one; none was found for the Southern Switchyard drawn here.
notes.regulatory_context: The PG&E Southern Switchyard: one of two PG&E switchyards at the western end of the Potrero Power Station site (final D4D p.12, Figure 1.2.1), south of the 4.8-acre Northern Switchyard and north of the Transbay Cable site, outside the project site boundary; labelled 'SWITCHYARDS (PG&E)' on Figure 6.2.3, between Illinois Street and Georgia Lane beside Block 5. The 4.8-acre Northern Switchyard at 22nd and Illinois Streets, 'currently owned and operated by PG&E as an electrical switchyard' (SF Planning project page), is a different feature: it is within the 29-acre master plan and the project boundary, and the D4D sets standards for redevelopment of the entire PG&E Sub-area (this dataset represents that area as Blocks 13 and 14). For the Southern Switchyard drawn here, 'outside the project site boundary' is the D4D's statement; the 1990s CPUC divestiture EIR describes a switchyard in the southwest portion of the plant site along the east side of Illinois Street that 'is not part of the sale, and will be retained by PG&E'. Recorded as existing on the strength of the February 2020 D4D showing it; no more recent source was found. 'Commercial' is the nearest category in this map's use list; the feature is an electrical switchyard, a utility use (the D4D's 'Utility and Infrastructure' category), and the map has no utility category.

facts.value: Not stated in any source found for the Southern Switchyard drawn on this record's map; the approximately 4.8 acres in the D4D and on SF Planning's project page is the Northern Switchyard at 22nd and Illinois

The D4D (p.12, Figure 1.2.1 Site Boundaries and Ownership) shows two PG&E switchyards at the western end of the Power Station: the 'PG&E Northern Switchyard (4.8 acres)', within the project site's boundary at the corner of 22nd and Illinois Streets, and the 'PG&E Southern Switchyard', which is not within the boundary and lies to the north of the Transbay Cable site. This record's map polygon is the Southern Switchyard. For the Northern Switchyard: it sits inside the dashed boundary of the overall ~29-acre planning area (21 developer-owned acres + this 4.8-acre PG&E parcel + 2.8 acres of Port/City land), was included in the project's planning and environmental clearance with PG&E's approval, but is not part of the Development Agreement's Developer Property; ultimate build-out depends on the switchyard's relocation and the site coming within the DA's legal jurisdiction.

PG&E has completed remediation of the PG&E sub-area portion of the former power plant site still under its ownership; the DEIR separately identifies 'PG&E switchyards to the west between Humboldt and 22nd streets' as an adjacent area also subject to PG&E remediation, independent of the project

Labeled 'SWITCHYARDS (PG&E)' on the D4D's Building Height Plan (Figure 6.2.3) and Land Use Plan (Figure 3.1.1), outside the dashed project site boundary, between Illinois Street and Georgia Lane and adjoining Block 5; the D4D's Figure 1.2.1 and p.12 identify this location as the Southern Switchyard

changes.text: The Design for Development shows two PG&E switchyards: a 4.8-acre Northern Switchyard at 22nd and Illinois inside the project boundary (covered on this map by Blocks 13 and 14), and a Southern Switchyard outside it. The shape on this record is the Southern one, so the record now says so: the 4.8-acre area and the 22nd and Illinois location were moved to the Northern Switchyard, the claim that it is outside the redevelopment site is limited to the Southern one, and the earlier comparison of the shape's area to 4.8 acres was withdrawn as coincidental. The shape itself was not changed. The dead 2019 draft link was replaced with the final February 2020 document, the label location was corrected to east of Illinois Street, and the land-use figure is tagged as a document rather than a rendering.

open_questions: No DataSF Assessor parcel matching the switchyard's shape or address was confirmed in any source found here, consistent with the accuracy note already recorded for this record's map shape; no source found gives the switchyard an address or APN.

No source found on the status, timeline, or cost of relocating the switchyard, or on any agreement between PG&E and the developer beyond PG&E's stated approval to include the parcel in planning and environmental review.
The DEIR's reference to 'PG&E switchyards' (plural, between Humboldt and 22nd Streets) may describe both the Northern and Southern switchyards; that identification is not independently confirmed.

The D4D's Figure 1.2.1 shows the 4.8-acre 'PG&E Northern Switchyard' inside the project boundary; this record's map polygon is the separate 'PG&E Southern Switchyard' outside it, and no acreage is stated for the Southern one. The Northern Switchyard is not drawn as its own feature here: this dataset's Blocks 13 and 14 cover that area. Whether to add or rename features is undecided.

No source found giving a construction or commissioning date for the PG&E Northern Switchyard itself (distinct from the power plant blocks it served); left without a dated 'became existing' milestone rather than forcing the redevelopment plan's own adoption date onto a structure that predates and is unrelated to that plan.
